en.help.title: Rust Language Server (rust-analyzer)
en.help.message:
rust-analyzer is Rust's language server: completion, diagnostics, hover, go-to-definition and refactoring come from it.

Install it with rustup (official, recommended) or Homebrew:
  rustup component add rust-analyzer
  brew install rust-analyzer

How gvim starts rust-analyzer:
  * This is a helper plugin: gvim's built-in Rust LSP entry starts rust-analyzer when a Rust file opens under the normal LSP rules (lsp_enabled, rust root markers such as Cargo.toml, auto_start).
  * An explicit "lsp" entry for rust in config.json replaces the built-in entry (and "enabled": false for rust disables it); explicit user configuration always wins.
  * These helper commands never start, stop or select the native Rust LSP server. Disable Rust LSP delegates to gvim's controlled native language-disable action: it re-checks the active .rs buffer/language and mutes that language at the LSP port for all Rust roots; it is not a server restart or a per-buffer setting, and the asynchronous result is native-owned.
  * Check rust-analyzer runs rust-analyzer --version through the workspace authority (remote included; the workspace trust gate may refuse it). Only a successful check (exit 0, no timeout or signal) counts: a non-zero exit, timeout or signal is a failed check. The plugin's local-only PATH lookup is never used for a presence decision.

If it is installed but gvim cannot find it:
  * run `rustup component add rust-analyzer` and then `rust-analyzer --version` in the same shell on the workspace host;
  * restart gvim (or Start/Restart LSP Server) after installing so PATH is re-read;
  * use the native Start/Restart LSP Server and Show LSP Status actions below to check the server state and logs;
  * a mismatched rust-analyzer/rustc toolchain can prevent startup: `rustup update` and check `rustup component list --installed`.

Docs: https://rust-analyzer.github.io/book/installation.html
